sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 10.0% a year from $129 billion in FY2017 to $303 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F203].

The window is not smooth: growth stepped up to 17.5% in FY2021 and 15.8% in FY2022, then fell back to 6.8% in FY2023 and 5.0% in FY2024 before re-accelerating to 10.1% in FY2026 [D189][D238][D287][D336][D434].
The FY2021 jump came from a 16% comparable sales increase and strong non-foods and e-commerce sales [P56][P54].
FY2022's 16% net sales increase was driven by 14% comparable sales, with gasoline, business centers and travel the fastest-growing businesses [P42].
The US segment supplied 72.5% of FY2026 revenue and contributed 7.2pp of the 10.1% growth, with Other International adding 1.6pp and Canada 1.3pp [D670][D672][D679][D686][D434].
FY2026's $27.3 billion net sales increase was primarily attributable to an 8% comparable sales rise, split 5% average ticket and 3% shopping frequency, plus 25 net new warehouses [P14].

Food and Sundries remained the largest product line at 38.5% of revenue but contributed only 2.6pp of FY2026 growth, while warehouse ancillary and other businesses added 3.7pp on 19.9% growth [D558][D560][D601][D600].
Operating income grew 12.5% against 10.1% revenue growth in FY2026, an incremental operating margin of 4.7% [D435][D434][D457].
Operating costs grew 0.1pp slower than revenue in FY2026, with cost of revenue up 10.2% and SG&A up 8.9% [D458][D449][D450].
Operating margin reached a window high of 3.9% in FY2026 against a 3.4% median and a 3.1% low in FY2019 [F32][D691][D692][D690].
The FY2026 margin rose 0.1pp, with SG&A adding 0.1pp and cost of revenue flat at 87.2% of revenue [D447][D460][D459][D413].
SG&A fell 10 basis points as a share of net sales, though excluding gasoline price inflation it rose one basis point, with foreign currency adding $126 million [P9].
In FY2026 net margin of 3.0% sat 0.8pp below the 3.9% operating margin, a gap the pack puts at -0.8pp [F52][F32][D732].
Operating cash flow of $15.8 billion was 1.71x net income in FY2026, above the 1.75x window median's level and well above the 1.26x FY2022 low [F82][F42][D421][D722][D721].
The increase was primarily due to higher operating income and reduced net investment in merchandise inventories from faster turns and improved supplier payment terms [P6].
Free cash flow of $9.4 billion was 1.02x net income and a 3.1% margin, against a 2.8% window median [F102][F42][D422][D418][D698].
Capex of $6.4 billion was 2.1% of revenue and 2.41x D&A, the highest multiple in the window [F92][F10][D417][D423].
Net cash reached $15.1 billion, or 5.0% of revenue, in FY2026 from net debt of $880 million in FY2017 [D427][D428][D15].
That net cash position ranks at the 100th percentile of four retail peers, against a peer median of -18.3% of revenue [D733][D734].
Buybacks and dividends of $3.3 billion absorbed 35.2% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count was essentially flat at 444.4 million [D429][D430][X100].
FY2026 repurchases of 891,000 shares cost $847 million, leaving $1,115 million under the January 2023 authorization [P3].
Operating margin of 3.9% sits at the 17th percentile of six retail peers against a 5.0% median, and net margin of 3.0% also ranks 17th against 3.5% [F32][D709][D710][F52][D711][D712].
The thin-margin model is structural rather than deteriorating, since the margin is at its window high, but it leaves little cushion if merchandise costs or wages move against the company.
Capex has grown 11.1% a year against 10.0% revenue growth, lifting capex to 2.41x D&A from 1.83x in FY2017 [F209][F203][D423][D11].
Rising capital intensity is the main claim on the growing free cash flow, and the filings tie the spend to new and remodeled warehouses rather than to any disclosed return target.
Whether operating margin holds at the FY2026 high of 3.9% or slips toward the 3.4% window median, reported in the FY2027 10-K [F32][D692].
Whether free cash flow margin stays at or above the 2.8% window median from FY2026's 3.1%, in the FY2027 10-K [D418][D698].
Whether warehouse ancillary and other businesses repeat FY2026's 19.9% growth or revert toward the 2.4% of FY2025, in the FY2027 10-K [D600][D597].
